ranked_facts.concept_key: ECG findings with ST-segment elevations and PR-segment depression
ranked_facts.why: The ECG findings of ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression in leads II, III, and aVF are more characteristic of myopericarditis than of STEMI, which typically presents with ST-segment elevations without PR-segment depression.
An elevated serum troponin I level is consistent with myopericarditis, which can cause myocardial injury, but is not typically seen in pulmonary embolism.
